Fluency/quality measured independently — perplexity, LLM-judge Likert or win-rate, and in the stronger papers a human panel (Sadasivan: 20 passages × 3 MTurk raters; Krishna App. C.2; Lu et al., TMLR 2024, human readability + task-completion for SICO).
At least one downstream-utility check that the attacked text still does its job (Sadasivan's SQuAD-v2 QA retention at 97%).
A no-attack and a weak-attack baseline so the marginal contribution of the proposed attack is visible (plain paraphrase vs the proposed method).
Multiple generator/attacker models and multiple domains, because RAID's headline finding is that single-model, single-domain detector results do not transfer.
The reverse error direction — spoofing human text into an AI verdict — reported alongside evasion when the paper draws an institutional conclusion (Sadasivan; Perkins's FPR column).

A defense or recalibration analysis: does retraining, re-thresholding, or a second instrument recover the evaded texts (Krishna's retrieval defense; DAMAGE's augmented detector; RAID's leaderboard as a standing defense venue).
Public release of the attacked texts and code so third parties can re-score them against detectors the authors did not test, and re-score after vendor updates.
Per-attack and per-condition breakdown tables rather than a single pooled headline rate.
we_meet: Threat model stated at a precision the literature rarely reaches: the access ladder is named explicitly and the target detector is never queried during search — only at submission — with the pre-2022 human exemplars justified as archive-obtainable rather than detector-derived (§4.9, `BYPASS_METHODOLOGY.md`).

Attack budget stated and the single-submission rate separated from the best-of-N rate, exactly Sadasivan's pp-N vs 'best of' distinction: per-variant 11.1% [5.5, 17.6] (one blind submission) vs per-target 22.5% [14.4, 33.5] (≤18 attempts, 6 rounds × 3 variants).
A no-attack/weak-attack baseline exists and runs the right way: a plain 'make this sound human' prompt *raises* Pangram's score, so the ladder's bottom rung is not silently omitted.
The spoofing direction is instrumented — human text pushed through the same ladder moved 11.7 → 60.2 on the AI score — which most evasion papers omit entirely.

A same-detector specificity anchor stronger than any published comparator: 0 AI verdicts in 1,260 genuine pre-2022 controls, so the reversals are movements into a class the detector otherwise never reaches.

Uncertainty quantification that exceeds the field: a text-clustered bootstrap (20,000 draws, design effect 3.40, effective n ≈ 100 of 341) instead of the naive Wilson interval the literature would have printed, and the naive interval shown for contrast.

Denominator discipline stricter than field practice: the 6 of 71 targets that never produced a submittable variant are counted as attack failures, and the alternative conditional rate (24.6%) is disclosed rather than quoted.

In-sample and out-of-sample rates separated: NB v3's 25.0% is flagged as partly protocol-fitted, GO all-31's 19.4% named as the clean out-of-sample point, with the honest replication expectation stated as ≈19–22%.
Superseded biased runs quarantined to Appendix B with their pooled effect on the number (8.5% vs 11.1%) stated in the open.

Detector-instability reporting the vendor literature does not do: 11% label/score disagreement on re-scan in one chamber (`ga033` Mixed at fraction_ai 0.67, `ga092` Human at 0.10) vs 30/30 at exactly 0.0 in the other; both label and continuous score reported throughout.

Quality of the attacked text measured on two complementary selections — selection-on-proxy (stages 3/4, 63 blinded within-text pairs) and selection-on-outcome (stage 5, the 39 successful reversals, two passes, 79–100% inter-pass agreement) — all seven DQI dimensions null, with minimum detectable effects (±0.12–0.26) stated instead of null-as-proof.

A cross-instrument check on the attacked texts already exists: the register ruler scores AUC 0.535 on the evasion variants (`register_auc_check.py`), i.e. the attack is shown to defeat the second, detector-independent instrument as well.

The incommensurability of the vendor comparison is named in the text before a referee can name it: ground truth is a Pangram verdict on the original rather than known authorship, and only the per-variant row is offered as commensurable with the vendor FNR rows.

Committed, reproducible scripts for every number, and the vendor benchmark assembled into one table (Pangram 4 clean 0.34%, 13 humanizers 2.31%, BLADER 0.43%, Epoch Style Imitation 2.86%) with each row's provenance labelled as vendor-reported on undisclosed data.

gaps.gap: One target detector. Every accepted work in this literature attacks 4–12 detectors across families (Krishna 5, Sadasivan 4 families, Cheng 8, RAID 12, Perkins 6, Weber-Wulff 14). S10's claim as written — 'detection is a norm-measurement tool, not a security control' — generalizes from n=1 commercial vendor, and a referee will say the result may be a fact about Pangram 4's decision surface rather than about detection.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Re-score all 341 evasion variants and their 71 originals on at least three additional detectors: Binoculars (Hans et al. 2024) and Fast-DetectGPT (Bao et al. 2024) computed from the open-model log-probs S10 already holds, plus one supervised baseline (OpenAI RoBERTa-Large or MAGE) and ideally one other commercial API (GPTZero or Originality). Report a per-detector evasion table and, since the Opus self-score is the guiding signal, a guiding-vs-target transfer statement in Cheng et al.'s form.
gaps.feasibility: Binoculars and Fast-DetectGPT are computable now from held data — the pipeline already runs open-model log-probs (§4.7) and §7 already discusses both detectors. A second commercial API costs ~341 document calls (tens of dollars). No new text collection.

gaps.gap: Ground truth is the detector's own prior verdict, not known machine authorship, so the headline is an induced label-reversal rate and not an FNR — which is precisely the quantity the 2.31% and 0.34% vendor rows are. S10 says this, but saying it does not make the ratio commensurable, and the '~10×' rests on the ratio.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Re-run the frozen search on text with known machine authorship: the 40 open-model-generated speeches from §4.1 that Pangram flagged 40/40 are the obvious seed set, extended to ~100 by generating more in the same way. The resulting rate is a true adversarial FNR on known-AI text and is directly comparable to Pangram's 0.34% / 2.31% / 2.86% rows without a paragraph of caveat.
gaps.feasibility: Fully computable from data S10 holds plus routine generation and API scoring; the generation harness and Pangram scoring path already exist. A few hundred dollars of API and a day of compute.

gaps.gap: The '~10× the commercial evasion baseline' compares S10's own measurement on legislative speech against Pangram's self-reported number on Pangram's undisclosed test set, under a different accounting (one humanizer pass vs up to 18 attempts) and a different text length and domain. DAMAGE — the same lab — shows the same humanizers getting 40% past GPTZero and 72% past Binoculars, so 'commercial humanizers achieve 2.31%' is a Pangram-vs-Pangram fact. No referee in this literature will accept a vendor-vs-us ratio when the comparator is purchasable.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Run two to four commercial humanizers (Undetectable AI, StealthGPT, Phrasly, HIX Bypass — the DAMAGE inventory) over the same 71 targets, one pass each, and score with Pangram 4. That produces a same-texts, same-detector, same-accounting humanizer baseline; the '10×' then becomes a within-experiment ratio with its own interval, or gets corrected.
gaps.feasibility: New collection, but trivial: ~$100 of subscriptions and one day. The targets, the scoring path and the verdict criteria all already exist.

gaps.gap: No success-versus-budget curve and no cost per successful evasion. The field treats budget as a first-class axis (Krishna caps at one pass to avoid inflating; Sadasivan reports pp1–pp5 separately; RAID applies each attack once). S10 quotes a ceiling (≤18 attempts) but not the distribution, so a reader cannot tell whether 22.5% is reached at round 2 or only at round 6, and cannot price the attack.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: From the existing run logs, plot cumulative success rate against attempt index (1…18) with the clustered bootstrap at each point, and report the median round of first success plus tokens and dollars per successful evasion. This also converts the per-variant/per-target pair from two points into the curve that connects them.
gaps.feasibility: Pure re-analysis of held run artifacts; the round index of every submission is already recorded. Hours.

gaps.gap: Semantic fidelity of the evasion is never measured. The DQI arms grade deliberative quality, not whether the rewrite still says what the member said — the field's minimum is a similarity instrument against a human-paraphrase reference (Krishna's P-SP) plus a downstream-utility check (Sadasivan's SQuAD-v2 retention). For this threat model it is load-bearing: a rewrite that drops the bill number, the constituent's name, or the commitment is not a speech the member could have delivered, and every such case inflates the rate.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: On the 38 successful variants and their originals: embedding/NLI similarity or P-SP against the distribution of human paraphrase pairs; named-entity, numeral and date retention rates; and a QA-retention test — generate 5 factual questions per original speech, answer them from the variant, report accuracy. Report the evasion rate again restricted to variants passing a pre-stated fidelity floor.
gaps.feasibility: Fully computable from held text with no new collection; the LLM-grading harness already exists. The fidelity-floor-restricted rate is the number a referee will want as the headline.

gaps.gap: No human evaluation anywhere in the evasion arm, while the attacker and both graders are Claude models — and the draft already records r = +0.758 between two supposedly independent AI judges. The two strongest comparators both ran human panels (Sadasivan 20 × 3 MTurk; Lu et al. TMLR 2024 human readability and task-completion for SICO). A referee will read 'quality unchanged' as 'Claude says Claude's rewrite is fine'.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: A small blinded human panel: ~60 original/variant pairs, 3 raters each, judging (a) would this pass as a floor speech in this chamber, (b) does it preserve the original's content, (c) forced-choice which is machine-drafted. Report agreement with the DQI rubric and with the Pangram verdict.
gaps.feasibility: New collection but small — a Prolific/MTurk panel is a few hundred dollars and a week. Ideally at least a handful of raters with parliamentary familiarity for (a).

gaps.gap: One attacker model (Opus) and no weak-attack rung between 'plain prompt' and the full contrastive ladder. RAID's headline finding is that single-generator results do not transfer; Krishna's whole design varies the generator. As it stands, '~1 in 5' may be an Opus fact.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Replicate the frozen search on a ~25-target subsample with a different attacker family (a GPT or Gemini frontier model, and one open-weights model), and add an off-the-shelf paraphrase rung — DIPPER (public) or a single plain paraphrase pass — over all 71 targets to give the attack ladder its bottom step and quantify the marginal value of the contrastive apparatus.
gaps.feasibility: New inference on existing texts, no new collection. DIPPER weights are public; the subsample keeps API cost small.

gaps.gap: Everything is reported at Pangram's default categorical operating point, so nothing in the arm is commensurable with the TPR@1%FPR / accuracy@5%FPR convention that every comparator uses, and the obvious defense question goes unanswered: could a re-thresholded detector catch the 38 reversals, and at what specificity cost on the 1,260 controls?
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Using the continuous fraction_ai already recorded for every variant, control and prevalence segment, sweep the threshold: plot evasion rate vs threshold and the induced false-positive rate on the 1,260 pre-2022 controls at each point; state the evasion rate at the threshold that holds control FPR at 1% and at 5%. Add the analogous curve for the register instrument (its 0.535 AUC on variants is already computed).
gaps.feasibility: Pure re-analysis of held scores. Hours. This is also the field-required 'defense/recalibration' element and answers it cheaply.

gaps.gap: 71 targets, CI [14.4, 33.5] — the interval spans a factor of 2.3, and the two chambers' 4.1-point gap carries a [−17, +25] interval. Comparators run 805 documents (Perkins), 6M generations (RAID), hundreds per condition (Sadasivan). The out-of-sample point that carries the claim rests on 31 targets.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Extend the uniform-draw arm to ~200 targets pooled and, more valuably, run the frozen v3 protocol pre-registered on a third chamber (UK Commons or Dáil, both scored entirely on Pangram 4) to give a genuinely out-of-sample replication rather than a second in-sample chamber.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data — the flagged-segment pool is 37,801 scored segments — plus Pangram API spend and search compute. The only true cost is money and wall-clock.

gaps.gap: The measured scenario is 'rewrite a speech the detector already flagged', not the realistic institutional workflow 'draft a speech that will not be flagged'. The security-control conclusion is about the second, and it is untested. Conditioning on high-confidence AI flags may also make the targets systematically harder than fresh evade-aware drafts.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Generate ~100 fresh speeches on real chamber topics under an evade-aware prompt (with and without the contrastive exemplars), score with Pangram 4, and report the flag rate against the 9.03% prevalence figure and against the 0.34% clean FNR. This is the number a chamber's standards committee would actually ask for.
gaps.feasibility: New generation on existing topic/context data; the generation and scoring harness both exist. Cheap.

gaps.gap: Spoofing is present as a mean-shift anecdote (human text 11.7 → 60.2) rather than as a rate, though it is the error direction that determines whether a chamber can use the detector at all — and it is the direction Perkins and Weber-Wulff make institutional policy on.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Report how many of the ladder-processed genuine human speeches crossed to a Mixed or AI verdict, out of how many, with the same clustered interval; and separately the false-positive rate on unedited pre-2022 controls (already 0/1,260) so both error directions appear in one table.
gaps.feasibility: Held data if the ladder-processed human texts were scored by Pangram; if only Opus-scored, ~40 additional API calls. Hours to a day.

gaps.gap: No third-party-rescorable artifact release. RAID's standing contribution is that its attacked texts can be re-scored by anyone against detectors and detector versions the authors never saw; DAMAGE and humanizer evaluations both note detectors get patched against known attacks. S10 already documents 11% verdict instability on re-scan, which makes persistence a live question rather than a formality.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Publish the 341 variants with their originals, verdicts, fraction_ai scores and round indices as a dataset; re-score the 38 successes on the next Pangram version and report the persistence rate as a dated row.
gaps.feasibility: Release is immediate from held artifacts (subject to Hansard licensing, which is public record). Persistence needs elapsed time and one vendor update — schedule it rather than block on it.

gaps.gap: No length stratification, though Pangram's document-level FNRs are length-sensitive and legislative segments span a wide word range; the vendor comparison rows are essay-length documents. If evasion success concentrates in short segments the headline rate is partly a length artifact and partly not comparable to the vendor rows at all.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Evasion rate by word-count quartile with clustered intervals, and the same for the vendor-comparable per-variant row restricted to segments in the length band the vendor benchmark uses.
gaps.feasibility: Held data; word counts are already in the segment table. Hours.

gaps.gap: The cross-instrument result is buried in a methods aside. The register ruler scores AUC 0.535 on the evaded variants — i.e. the attack defeats the detector-independent instrument too. That is directly load-bearing on the paper's own architecture (it means the 9.03% floor argument applies to the register measurement as well, not just to Pangram) and referees will find it if the authors do not surface it.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Move the register-under-attack number into the bypass section as a named result, with the register's score distribution for originals vs successful variants vs controls, and state explicitly what it does and does not do to the floor claim.
gaps.feasibility: Already computed (`register_auc_check.py`, 292 final-run bypass variants). Editorial, not analytical.

surveys.verdict: On internal rigor S10 clearly exceeds the published evasion literature — threat-model precision, a stated attack budget with single-pass and best-of rates separated, failures kept in the denominator, text-clustered bootstrap intervals, in-sample/out-of-sample separation, quarantined pilot runs, blinded quality grading on both proxy-selected and outcome-selected variants, and detector-instability reporting are all things Krishna, Sadasivan, RAID and Cheng mostly do not do — but on the breadth the field actually gates acceptance on it falls short: one detector with no transferability check, one attacker model, detector-label rather than known-authorship ground truth, 71 targets, no semantic-fidelity or human evaluation of the evasions, and a headline "~10×" that divides an own-measurement by a vendor self-report on different texts under a different protocol; the narrow claim ("a directed blind search walked ~1 in 5 flagged Pangram-4 speeches to a Human verdict") is over-evidenced by field norms, while the general claim ("detection is not a security control") is currently under-evidenced by them, and the three blocking gaps are all closable from data S10 already holds plus roughly a week and a few hundred dollars.

nearest_works.work: Hiromu Yakura, Ezequiel Lopez-Lopez, Levin Brinkmann, Ignacio de la Serna, Lara Kirfel, Prateek Gupta, Ivan Soraperra, Thomas F. Eisenmann, Dirk U. Wulff, Iyad Rahwan — "Empirical evidence of Large Language Model's influence on human spoken communication"
nearest_works.venue_year: arXiv:2409.01754 (v1 Sep 2024, v4 Jul 2026); MPI Center for Humans and Machines; widely covered (Scientific American) but still a preprint, not peer-reviewed
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: ChatGPT-preferred words (delve, comprehend, boast, swift, meticulous) entered spontaneous human SPEECH after Nov 2022 — the same claim shape as S10's permeation claim, i.e. machine register moving into human production, not machine drafting.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: (1) Word list derived model-side, not by hand: ChatGPT edits of human text across 7 corpora and 4 model versions, log-odds ratios aggregated into a Bayesian-hierarchical 'GPT score'. (2) 740,249 h / 360,445 YouTube academic videos + 771,591 podcast episodes, ALL re-transcribed with WhisperX because YouTube changed its ASR model ~2020 (instrument-drift control). (3) Spontaneity enforced by construction: pyannote diarization, >=2 speakers and >=4 exchanges; 25-84% of episodes discarded. (4) Synthetic control per word against THREE donor pools (GPT-score-zero word2vec neighbours; 100 synonyms; 100 random) plus a piecewise-linear DiD with a Nov-2022 changepoint. (5) In-time placebo tests confirming specificity to Nov 2022; post/pre MSPE-ratio permutation against the donor distribution. (6) Dose-response two ways: by domain AI-uptake (delve significant in Science&Tech p=.03, Business p=.04, Education p=.04; null in Religion p=.29, Sports p=.66) and word-level GPT-score vs post-release trend change. (7) A preregistered individual-level experiment (N=496) showing chatbot exposure -> adoption surviving a distractor task. (8) Effects in interpretable units: ~25-50% per-year growth.

nearest_works.work: Bryce Anderson, Riley Galpin, Tom S. Juzek — "Model Misalignment and Language Change: Traces of AI-Associated Language in Unscripted Spoken English"
nearest_works.venue_year: AIES 2025 (Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society), Oct 2025; arXiv:2508.00238
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: A moderate but significant post-2022 rise in LLM-associated words in UNSCRIPTED spoken English — convergence of human word choice on LLM-associated patterns.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: 22.1M words of unscripted conversational science/tech podcast speech; pre- vs post-Dec-2022 lexical trends on delve, intricate, surpass, boast, meticulous, strategically, garner, underscore; the load-bearing control is NEAR-SYNONYM BASELINES scored identically (underscore vs accentuate) which show no significant directional shift; explicit refusal to claim causation ('open question whether AI is amplifying conventional patterns of language change or directly driving them'). The same group's extension (Juzek, arXiv:2605.25358, May 2026, WMT News Crawl, 34 languages) repeats the design with matched baseline words: -4.5% for baselines vs +15.1% for AI-associated lemmas, and compares post-2022 shifts against earlier periods.

nearest_works.work: Jane Stuart-Smith, Gwilym Pryce, Claire Timmins, Barrie Gunter — "Television can also be a factor in language change: Evidence from an urban dialect"
nearest_works.venue_year: Language 89(3):501-536, 2013 (with David Sayers, "The mediated innovation model", Journal of Sociolinguistics 18(2):185-212, 2014 as the standard-setting critique, and Stuart-Smith 2017 review, Glasgow eprint 131091)
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: A non-contact source (broadcast TV) is a real factor in the diffusion of TH-fronting and L-vocalisation into Glasgow vernacular — the canonical 'a register/feature is permeating speech from a source that is not face-to-face contact' claim, and the one the field spent 20 years refusing to accept without individual-level evidence.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: 48 individually interviewed speakers (36 adolescents in three age bands, 12 adults 40-60, balanced by sex) with a per-informant demographic/social/attitudinal/media questionnaire; media EXPOSURE and psychological ENGAGEMENT entered as separate predictors in one large multifactorial regression alongside competing causes (dialect contact with friends/family in England, local street-style social practices, linguistic-internal factors); the decisive result is the dose distinction — raw exposure null or negative, only strong para-social engagement (EastEnders as favourite programme, favourite characters, criticising storylines) significant. Plus: a negative-control set of variables never linked to London English (three vowels, /r/) that show no media effect; a source-side comparison showing EastEnders characters' phonetics and constraints against Glasgow adolescents' (which ruled OUT direct copying); an imitation task and an embedded TV-quiz-show exposure experiment as the mechanism leg; and an 18-month media embargo to suppress demand effects. Effects reported as one factor among several, ranked below linguistic-internal factors.

nearest_works.work: Jacob Eisenstein, Brendan O'Connor, Noah A. Smith, Eric P. Xing — "Diffusion of Lexical Change in Social Media"
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: Lexical innovations diffuse along identifiable channels — the standard for turning 'word X is spreading' into 'word X is spreading THROUGH this population by this route'.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: 107M tweets from 2.7M accounts with geolocation and time; a latent vector-autoregressive model aggregating thousands of words to estimate directed city-to-city influence rather than mere co-movement; competing structural predictors tested against each other (geographic proximity, population size, demographic similarity) with the finding that racial-demographic similarity dominates distance. The lesson the field took: a diffusion claim is judged by whether the adopting population's structure is modelled, not by whether the aggregate frequency rose.

nearest_works.work: Dmitry Kobak et al. — "Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary"
nearest_works.venue_year: Science Advances 11, eadt3813, 2025 (doi 10.1126/sciadv.adt3813); code/word list at github.com/berenslab/llm-excess-vocab
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: A lower bound on LLM-assisted text (>=13.5% of 2024 PubMed abstracts, up to 40% in subcorpora) from excess vocabulary alone — this is the instrument S10 borrows and runs as a fixed ruler.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: 15M abstracts, 2010-2024; counterfactual frequencies extrapolated from pre-LLM years so 'excess' is defined against a fitted baseline, not against an eyeballed trend; 900 excess words released WITH annotations (style vs content) so per-word drivers are auditable; results broken out by discipline, country and journal with heterogeneity reported; the effect size benchmarked against a known real vocabulary shock in the same corpus (COVID) to make the magnitude legible; the estimate framed explicitly as a lower bound.

nearest_works.work: Mingmeng Geng, Roberto Trotta — "Human-LLM Coevolution: Evidence from Academic Writing"
nearest_works.venue_year: Findings of the ACL 2025, pp. 12689-12696, Vienna
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: The counter-hypothesis a referee will raise: marker-word trajectories are not a clean diffusion signal, because humans adapt — 'delve' frequency DROPPED sharply once it was publicly named in early 2024, while other ChatGPT-favoured words ('significant') kept rising.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: Word-frequency time series over arXiv abstracts at the individual-word level, showing divergent post-exposure trajectories within one word list; the inference is carried by per-word trajectories and their timing against a documented public event, not by a pooled effect. Establishes that pooled instrument-level effects hide sign-flipping components, and that any pooled register measure must be decomposed word by word before it is believed.

field_standard: A matched control/donor word set, scored by the identical pipeline, must move ~zero while the instrument words move — near-synonyms (Anderson/Galpin/Juzek), frequency- and semantics-matched donors (Yakura's three pools), or matched baselines with the contrast reported numerically (Juzek 2026: -4.5% vs +15.1%).
An in-time placebo: the same estimator on pre-treatment windows must be null, or, if it fires, the paper must reconcile that with the treatment claim explicitly and quantitatively.

Per-word trajectories reported alongside the pooled effect, with leave-one-word-out and an audit of topical/event drivers — pooled register effects hide sign-flipping components (Geng & Trotta; Kobak's annotated 900-word table).
Effects stated in interpretable units (per-million frequency, %/year) and benchmarked against a known real change of comparable size in the same corpus (Kobak's COVID benchmark; Yakura's 25-50%/yr).
The 'human' sample must be guaranteed unscripted by an explicit, auditable construction rule, not by assumption (Yakura's diarization filter discarding up to 84% of episodes).

An individual-level exposure or engagement measure entered alongside competing social predictors; aggregate co-movement of a trend with a treatment date is not accepted as diffusion evidence (Stuart-Smith et al.; Sayers 2014's central objection).

A dose-response gradient: the effect scales with exposure — by domain AI-uptake, by word-level model-preference score, or by individual engagement, with the null strata reported (Yakura's Sports/Religion nulls; Stuart-Smith's exposure-null/engagement-positive split).
Within-individual change separated from population turnover; an era contrast over a changing membership is compositionally confounded until a panel or fixed-effects cut says otherwise.
Competing diffusion routes measured and entered in the same model, not merely acknowledged (dialect contact vs media; geography/population/demographics in Eisenstein).

A source-side check: the putative source demonstrably carries the feature, and the match of constraints between source and adopter is examined (Stuart-Smith's EastEnders comparison ruled out direct copying).

Instrument stability across the observation window: transcription/measurement-regime changes documented and shown not to generate the trend (Yakura re-transcribed 740k hours because YouTube's ASR changed in 2020).
An individual-level causal leg where causation is claimed — a preregistered exposure experiment (Yakura N=496; Jakesch et al., CHI 2023) — or explicit downgrading of the language to descriptive.

Replication across independent corpora, domains or languages, with heterogeneity reported rather than pooled away (Yakura: YouTube + podcasts; Kobak: disciplines/countries/journals; Juzek 2026: 34 languages).
Small effects with many analysis forks carry a specification curve or preregistration; a bootstrap bound whose value depends on the seed is not reported as an interval.
we_meet: In-time placebo, run and reported: the pre-LLM window (2018-19 vs 2021-01 to 2022-11-29, 2020 dropped as buffer) yields +0.0150, permutation p = 0.017, and S10 states the reconciliation the field demands — this arm claims the drift itself in a window where no machine cause existed, unlike the lexicon arm S10 demoted for firing while attributing an LLM cause.

Contamination defeated by design rather than by argument: the headline permeation number comes from a window in which machine drafting is impossible, which is the strongest available answer to 'you are measuring drafting, not permeation' — the confound Yakura had to attack with diarization and Anderson et al. with corpus selection.

Detector-independence: the instrument routes through open-model in-context log-probs, not through Pangram, so the permeation claim does not inherit the detector's training-data blind spots (the exact objection S10's own §7 raises against Suvanto et al.'s glass-box classifier).

Scorer-invariance as a partial instrument-stability check: two model families agree on sign, on magnitude (+0.0118 Qwen3 vs +0.0081 Mistral) and on 9 of 10 cells, so the result is not one model's lexical preference.

Cluster-aware inference with the right unit: clustered bootstrap plus a permutation test shuffling era labels within chamber x family (3,000 draws), with agreement across routes (P(<=0) 0.017-0.024, permutation p 0.015-0.022 across seeds).

Honest replication accounting rarely seen in the nearest works: S10 states that the 10 cells are two scorers of one text sample, not ten replications, and lets the permutation test rather than the sign count carry the inference.

Honest precision: the interval is quoted as ~[0.000, +0.020] because the bootstrap's lower endpoint moves by an order of magnitude across seeds (+0.0001 to +0.0009 at B=2,000) — the discipline field standard item 14 asks for, applied to the reported interval.

Source-side provenance stronger than any nearest work: §4.7 shows the register is installed by post-training (pooled base->instruct +0.387, three model families), so the putative machine source is shown to carry the feature and the stage that produces it is named — Stuart-Smith's source-model check, done model-side.
Self-normalisation within trace, which absorbs corpus-wide fluency/likelihood drift that would otherwise masquerade as a register effect.

A level-series companion (§4.5, rise beginning 1994-96) that supplies the raw-frequency reading of the same words, which the field's excess-vocabulary designs (Kobak, Juzek) use as their primary evidence layer.

gaps.gap: No matched control-word set. S10 states outright: 'no placebo word list, no external control.' This is the single most standard test in this literature — every nearest work carries it (Yakura's three donor pools, Anderson/Galpin/Juzek's near-synonym baselines, Juzek 2026's -4.5% vs +15.1% matched contrast). Without it, a referee's default reading of a +0.01 in-context log-prob shift is that models' in-context likelihoods for ANY moderately formal word drift across a 1994-2026 corpus as topic, phrasing conventions and sentence length change; self-normalisation does not exclude this because it normalises the trace, not the word class.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Build a donor set matched to each Kobak instrument word on Hansard frequency decile, token length, POS and (ideally) embedding neighbourhood, excluding any word with a positive LLM prevalence ratio in the public Kobak/Juzek tables; rescore the identical occurrences with word_context_delta.py; report the donor-set era delta and the instrument-minus-donor difference-in-differences with the same permutation test. The claim needs donor ~0 and the DiD to survive.
gaps.feasibility: Fully computable from data S10 holds. The scoring path exists; donor lists come from Hansard's own frequency table plus the public berenslab/llm-excess-vocab word list. Cost is GPU re-scoring, not collection.

gaps.gap: The era contrast cannot distinguish within-member drift from membership turnover, and S10's own §4.6 makes turnover the leading rival: birth year is reported as the dominant simple correlate of the register, and cohorts formed inside the drift arrive over time. Mechanically, a chamber can show a rising pooled register level with every individual member perfectly static. Variationist referees treat the real-time/apparent-time distinction as the first question asked of any diffusion claim, and this is the version of it that bites hardest here.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Recompute the pooled delta on the balanced sub-panel of members with >=K scored occurrences in BOTH windows, with member fixed effects; then decompose the aggregate era delta into (a) within-member change, (b) entrant-minus-leaver composition, (c) interaction. Report both numbers. If the effect is entirely (b), the sentence 'the register is permeating human speech' must become 'the composition of speakers is shifting toward register-heavy cohorts'.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data — member IDs and the 1994-2026 panel are already in hand; it is a re-cut of the committed occurrence log-probs, no new collection.

gaps.gap: Spontaneity is not guaranteed by construction, and the two windows may differ in genre mix. The late pre-LLM window (2021-01 to 2022-11) overlaps hybrid/remote sittings in several chambers, a period that mechanically increased reading from prepared text. Yakura discarded up to 84% of episodes to buy the spontaneity guarantee; S10's permeation arm appears to run on the pooled record. A genre-composition shift between windows would produce exactly this sign.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Recompute the pre-LLM delta within genre using §4.3's genre ladder; post-stratify to a fixed genre mix; report the effect on the most spontaneous genres alone (interjections, questions, points of order); add window-boundary sensitivity that excludes remote-sitting periods and shifts the late window to 2019 or to 2022 only.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data — genre labels already exist from the §4.3 concentration analysis.

gaps.gap: No specification curve for an effect whose bootstrap lower bound already moves by an order of magnitude with the resampling seed. The forks are numerous and consequential: window boundaries, the buffer year, the 5-chamber subset, occurrence-count thresholds, the self-normalisation choice, model families, and the Kobak word list itself. The field became strict about this precisely because word-level LLM signals proved fragile (Geng & Trotta).
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: A multiverse over >=100 specifications crossing those forks; report the fraction of specifications with positive sign, the distribution of the point estimate, and the specifications that flip it. This is also the honest place to record how many instruments were tried before this one (the demoted lexicon arm is already in the paper and should be named in the curve's narrative).
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data; cheap — it is repeated invocation of an existing script.

gaps.gap: Pooled-only reporting with no per-word decomposition. Kobak released 900 excess words with annotations; Geng & Trotta showed that within one word list some words rise while others collapse. A pooled +0.0099 carried by three words with obvious Hansard-topical drivers is a different paper from one where 40 of 50 words move together — and a referee cannot tell which S10 has.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Per-word era deltas with confidence intervals; leave-one-word-out on the pooled estimate; count of individually positive words; a flag on words with plausible policy-topic drivers in Hansard, and a re-run with those dropped. Also report the per-word pre-LLM slopes to see whether the 1994-96 onset is a whole-class shift or a few lexical items.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data; cheap. This is the check most likely to change the conclusion, so it should be run before the claim is defended.

gaps.gap: No dose-response of any kind. Every nearest work that made a diffusion claim credible carries a gradient: Yakura's domain-uptake heterogeneity with reported nulls (Sports p=.66) and word-level GPT-score gradient, Stuart-Smith's exposure-null/engagement-positive split. S10 reports one pooled number and a sign count. Absent a gradient, the effect is a level shift co-occurring with time, which is what Sayers (2014) formalised as insufficient.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Two versions, both concrete. (a) Word-level: regress the per-word era delta on that word's LLM prevalence ratio from the public Kobak/Juzek tables — this is Yakura's Fig 3B and is the field's canonical gradient. (b) Member/chamber-level for the post-2022 half: use Pangram drafting share as an exposure proxy and test whether drift in a member's detector-NEGATIVE, unscripted speech scales with drafting intensity in their chamber/party/own scripted output. Report null strata rather than suppressing them.
gaps.feasibility: (a) fully computable from held data. (b) computable from held data but identifies only post-2022 and re-introduces detector dependence, so it strengthens rather than carries.

gaps.gap: No non-parliamentary control corpus for the pre-LLM drift — the claim's most distinctive assertion. If formal spoken English generally drifted toward this register from the mid-1990s, or if the drift is an artifact of transcription practice, then the 1994-96 onset is not a fact about legislatures. Kobak, Yakura and Juzek all replicate across corpora or domains as a matter of course.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Run the identical instrument on era-matched external spoken corpora: Spoken BNC1994 vs Spoken BNC2014 (the natural British comparison), the US Congressional Record as a second legislative arm, or COCA spoken 1994-2019. A null outside legislatures makes the finding institutional; a parallel rise makes it a general register shift, which is still publishable but is a different claim.
gaps.feasibility: Needs new collection, but the targets are standard and mostly obtainable — BNC1994/2014 and the Congressional Record are accessible; COCA requires a licence. Scoring cost is comparable to one chamber.

gaps.gap: Transcription and editorial-regime drift over 1994-2026 is unaddressed as an instrument confound. Hansard reporting conventions, verbatim policy, digitisation and (recently) ASR-assisted transcription changed repeatedly across the window, and every such change alters in-context likelihood at exactly the kind of connective/style words the Kobak list contains. This is the confound that forced Yakura to re-transcribe 740,000 hours after YouTube changed its ASR model around 2020.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Per-chamber structural-break tests on the register series with breakpoints estimated freely, checked against documented reporting-policy dates; a within-chamber discontinuity check at each known transition; and, for a recent slice where audio or video exists, an independently transcribed comparison against the official record. If a break coincides with a reporting change, that chamber's contribution to the 1994-96 onset must be discounted.
gaps.feasibility: Break tests computable from held data. The reporting-policy history needs new collection, but is the same kind of work as the 22-chamber disclosure-policy scan the team already completed.

gaps.gap: No competing pre-LLM cause is named or measured. A diffusion claim with no transmission route is the objection Sayers (2014) turned into a framework and Stuart-Smith answered with individual engagement measures. For a 1994-2022 register drift in legislatures the obvious rival is professionalisation — growth of member staff and press offices, centrally distributed party lines, and the spread of communications training — none of which involves any register 'permeating' anything.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Test whether the drift is concentrated in members with staffed offices or frontbench roles versus backbenchers (§4.6/D.4 already carries ministerial-office covariates); and add a cheap textual proxy for centrally supplied lines — near-duplicate phrasing recurring across same-party members within a short window — and test whether removing high-duplication speech removes the drift.
gaps.feasibility: Both computable from held data. Actual staffing budgets and press-office headcounts would need new collection and are the stronger version if the reviewer presses.

gaps.gap: The +0.01 effect has no field-legible unit, and its relationship to the paper's own §4.5 frequency series is not shown. Referees from this literature read effects in per-million-word rates or %/year (Yakura: 25-50%/yr; Juzek 2026: +15.1% vs -4.5%) and expect a benchmark against a known change in the same corpus (Kobak vs COVID).
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Convert the log-prob delta into an implied change in the probability of selecting a register word at the slot, and report the raw per-million frequency change of the same words across the same windows; then show convergent validity chamber by chamber between the §4.5 level series and the §4.8 in-context delta (do the chambers rank the same way?). Benchmark the magnitude against a vocabulary change in Hansard known to be real over the same window.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data; cheap. The convergent-validity table is the cheapest large credibility gain available to this arm.

gaps.gap: Adjacent prior art is not engaged, including one work whose title states S10's distinctive claim. Chang, 'Human writing and machine patterns: analyzing a decade of convergence', Scientometrics 2026 (doi 10.1007/s11192-026-05589-y) is by title the nearest published analysis of pre-LLM convergence toward machine patterns. Separately, Juzek 2026 (34 languages, WMT News Crawl) explicitly reports that post-2022 shifts EXCEED earlier periods, whereas S10 reports the reverse rate ordering in Hansard (~+0.0045/yr pre-LLM vs ~+0.0022/yr pre-to-post). A referee who knows this literature will read S10's ordering as an anomaly requiring explanation, not as a finding.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Acquire Chang 2026 and Juzek 2026; state the level-versus-acceleration distinction against their actual numbers rather than in the abstract; if Chang overlaps substantively, position S10 as extension rather than discovery (per the project's build-on-published-work convention). Where their corpora are public (WMT News Crawl is), run S10's in-context instrument on one of them as an external replication of the ordering.
gaps.feasibility: Acquisition plus a comparison paragraph is cheap; the external re-run is a modest new-collection task using public data.

gaps.gap: No individual-level causal leg, while the verb 'permeating' implies one. Yakura's v4 added a preregistered N=496 experiment showing chatbot exposure produces word adoption that survives a distractor; Jakesch et al. (CHI 2023) is the template for latent adoption from model output. S10 has no such evidence, and for the pre-LLM window no such experiment is even meaningful.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Either (a) an explicit framing discipline — for the pre-LLM window, never phrase the result as machines shaping humans, since S10's own claim is that the drift predates the models and has some other cause; and for the post-2022 half, state plainly that the design is descriptive-correlational; or (b) a small preregistered exposure experiment if a causal claim about the post-2022 half is wanted.
gaps.feasibility: (a) is free and should be done regardless. (b) needs new collection (online experiment, ~N=500), out of scope for a corpus paper; the cheaper substitute is the word-level dose-response in the dose-response gap.

surveys.verdict: S10's permeation arm meets or exceeds the field on inference hygiene and on the source side — detector-independence, a pre-LLM window where the drafting confound cannot exist, two agreeing scorer families, permutation plus clustered bootstrap with honest precision, and a base-versus-instruct provenance result stronger than any comparator's source check — but it falls short of the field's core identification bar on three items that every nearest work satisfies and that are computable from data S10 already holds: a matched control-word set (S10 states it has none, while Yakura, Anderson/Galpin/Juzek and Juzek 2026 all rest on one), separation of within-member drift from membership turnover (which S10's own birth-year finding makes the leading rival explanation), and a spontaneity/genre guarantee across the two windows; until those three are run, a competent referee will read the +0.01 as an unidentified corpus-composition effect rather than as permeation.

nearest_works.work: William Labov, The Social Stratification of English in New York City (and the crossover/hypercorrection chapters reprinted in Sociolinguistic Patterns)
nearest_works.venue_year: Center for Applied Linguistics, 1966 (2nd ed. Cambridge UP 2006); Sociolinguistic Patterns, U. Pennsylvania Press, 1972
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: The second-highest status group exceeds the highest on a prestige variable in formal styles (the crossover), driven by linguistic insecurity — the direct ancestor of S10's II-over-I result and of 'the top flees'.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: A stratified random sample of the Lower East Side (~88 analysed speakers) recorded across FIVE contextual styles (casual, careful, reading, word lists, minimal pairs), so the crossover is shown to appear specifically as monitoring rises; an independent rapid-anonymous replication in three department stores (Saks/Macy's/S. Klein, 264 interviews) using a store-status proxy collected separately; plus subjective-reaction and self-evaluation tests establishing that (r) carries prestige for the same speakers. Production, style, and evaluation are three separate instruments, and the claim rests on their agreement — not on production alone.

nearest_works.work: William Labov, Principles of Linguistic Change, Volume 2: Social Factors
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: The curvilinear hypothesis — innovation originates in interior (upper-working/lower-middle) social groups, not at the top or bottom — and the leaders of change are identifiable individuals.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: The Philadelphia Neighborhood Study: multiple communities sampled separately, a socioeconomic index built from occupation+education+residence, real-time resurveys, social-network position (density of local ties, proportion of weak ties), and named individual-level portraits of leaders whose trajectories are shown one by one. Crucially the claim is located both socially AND temporally: who leads is established by showing their curve precedes others' on the SAME variable, plus mathematical models of linear incrementation and cross-generational transmission.

nearest_works.work: Gillian Sankoff & Hélène Blondeau, 'Language change across the lifespan: /r/ in Montreal French'
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: Community-level change must be decomposed into cohort replacement versus change within individual lifespans; apparent-time and aggregate trend readings can misattribute one to the other.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: A paired TREND study (repeated community cross-sections) and PANEL study (the same 32 speakers re-recorded 1971→1984), analysed jointly. The finding — most individuals stable after adolescence, a sizeable minority changing substantially — is only visible because the same people are tracked. This paper is the reason a modern referee will not accept a group-mean era panel as evidence of dynamics.

nearest_works.work: Stanley Lieberson & Eleanor O. Bell, 'Children's First Names: An Empirical Study of Social Taste' (extended in Lieberson, A Matter of Taste)
nearest_works.venue_year: American Journal of Sociology 98(3): 511–554, 1992; A Matter of Taste, Yale UP, 2000
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: Discrete lexical markers (given names) diffuse down the status ladder and are abandoned by high-status parents once common — the exact analogue of S10's claim, on the exact same kind of marker.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: Complete New York State birth records 1973–1985 — a population, not a sample — with parental education and race attached to each individual adoption event. The diffusion claim is carried ITEM BY ITEM and LEAD-LAG: names entering the top-20 of high-education parents are shown to be adopted later by low-education parents, so direction is demonstrated by temporal precedence per name, not by a cross-sectional correlation over names.

nearest_works.work: Jonah Berger & Gaël Le Mens, 'How adoption speed affects the abandonment of cultural tastes'
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: Fast-rising cultural markers are abandoned faster — the abandonment half of a fashion cycle, stated as a dynamic law rather than a static signature.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: Over 100 years of first-name series in TWO countries (France and the US) — an independent-population replication — with per-item rise rate regressed on per-item subsequent decline rate; then an individual-level test showing expecting parents are more hesitant to adopt names with sharper recent increases; then experiments isolating the mechanism (perceived faddishness/symbolic value). Three levels — aggregate trajectory, individual adoption, causal mechanism — for one claim.

nearest_works.work: Alberto Acerbi, Stefano Ghirlanda & Magnus Enquist, 'The Logic of Fashion Cycles' (with the neutral-model program it sits in: Bentley, Hahn & Shennan, 'Random drift and culture change', Proc. R. Soc. B 271: 1443–1450, 2004; Acerbi & Bentley, Evolution and Human Behavior 35(3): 228–236, 2014; Newberry, Ahern, Clark & Plotkin, 'Detecting evolutionary forces in language change', Nature 551: 223–226, 2017)
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: Fashion-like rise-and-fall dynamics are a claim about turnover statistics that must be tested against unbiased copying, because random drift alone reproduces power-law popularity, turnover, and rise/fall correlations with no status mechanism whatever.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: An explicit generative model, simulated, whose predictions (power-law trait frequencies, correlation between a trait's rate of increase and its rate of decrease) are matched against real series — baby names, English colour terms, Last.fm listening — and the DEPARTURES from the neutral prediction are what license a bias claim. Newberry et al. supply the corpus-side version: a Wright–Fisher null and the Frequency Increment Test applied to diachronic corpora, with Karjus, Blythe, Kirby & Smith (Glossa 5(1): 45, 2020) showing such results are sensitive to how the corpus is binned in time — so binning robustness is now part of the expected package.

field_standard: The dependent measure must be a linguistic VARIABLE with a defined envelope of variation (Labov's accountability principle): rate per opportunity to use the form, not rate per 1,000 words, so that topic composition cannot generate the result.

Prestige/stigma must be established by evaluation evidence external to production — subjective-reaction, matched-guise, or self-evaluation tests (Labov 1966; Trudgill, Language in Society 1: 179–195, 1972) — before a usage difference may be read as status behaviour.

Status must be measured on an independent index built from non-linguistic facts (occupation, education, residence), ideally with a second orthogonal marker, and specified before the linguistic analysis.
Style stratification: the same speakers observed in more and less monitored contexts, with the prediction that a status display strengthens as monitoring rises.

Real time, not apparent time alone; and where real time exists, community change must be decomposed into cohort replacement versus within-individual lifespan change (Sankoff & Blondeau 2007; Bailey, Wikle, Tillery & Sand, Language Variation and Change 3: 241–264, 1991).

Individual-level trajectories — adoption and abandonment curves for persons, not group means — with rate parameters compared across strata (Labov 2001's named leaders; Berger & Le Mens 2009's individual hesitancy test; Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil et al., WWW '13, for the large-corpus version).

Direction of diffusion demonstrated ITEM BY ITEM as temporal precedence: the leading group's curve for a given marker must be shown to precede the following group's curve for that same marker (Lieberson & Bell 1992).

The abandonment half must be dynamic and conditional: high-status use of a specific item shown to FALL after that item becomes common, within group and within item — a hazard or event-study statement, not a cross-sectional correlation.

An explicit drift/neutral null: observed turnover, rise/fall asymmetry, and stratified differences must exceed what unbiased copying produces at matched corpus size and token counts (Bentley et al. 2004; Acerbi & Bentley 2014; Newberry et al. 2017), with sensitivity to temporal binning reported (Karjus et al. 2020).

Inference clustered on the speaker, with speaker and word/lemma as random effects; the speaker community is the unit of replication, not the token or the word type (Tagliamonte & Baayen, Language Variation and Change 24: 135–178, 2012).

Families of related tests reported with a joint or family-wise statistic — in this literature, a permutation test that reshuffles speaker-to-group assignment while preserving the correlation structure among words.
Independent replication in a second community collected separately (NYC→Philadelphia; France→US), not a re-slicing of the same corpus.
Null/abstention results supported by equivalence bounds and a stated minimum detectable effect, not by a non-significant coefficient.

Explicit control of the mechanical artifacts specific to frequency-change designs: shared-denominator coupling between a change score and the group whose counts feed it, regression to the mean in ratio measures, and topic drift.
we_meet: Real time, at a scale the anchor works do not have: a 1994–2026 continuous record over 22 chambers, which satisfies the field's hardest requirement (item 5's first half) outright — Labov, Lieberson and Berger all had to assemble real-time series precisely because production corpora of this depth did not exist for their variables.

An independent, pre-specified status index (item 3): EGP/NS-SEC coded from members' prior occupations, plus four further orthogonal markers — education level, office-holding, Wikipedia-article length across all 22 chambers (6,896 members, 99% coverage), and the preregistered organisational-altitude ladder. This exceeds the single socioeconomic index most of these works use.

A crossover result established by a design that needs no normalisation (item 12's spirit): class II over class I within each chamber, positive in 9 of 12, individually significant in all three chambers with power (UK +0.68 t=2.48; US House +0.82 t=2.10; Manitoba +2.26 t=2.21), inverse-variance meta z=3.50.

A negative control that discriminates the mechanism: the flight correlation reproduces at every top that is a status-top (professional degrees, executive rungs, office-holders) and runs flat-to-positive at the one top that is not (graduate degrees). None of the six anchor works offers a within-design falsification case this clean.
A dose-response: monotone strengthening of rho with the volume threshold (−0.13/−0.22/−0.42/−0.46), which is the shape a real effect emerging from noise attenuation would take.
The third predicted pattern — off-ladder abstention (free work flat at every threshold) — which is a genuine prediction of the Simmel/Veblen geometry and is not usually tested at all.
A partial version of item 8: §4.5's word-level peak-and-fall-back gives the abandonment dynamics for the marker set as a whole, independent of status.
The field's honesty norm, met explicitly: hypothesis-not-finding framing, stated non-independence of the robustness family, un-clustered SEs flagged in place, and peak location declared a non-claim.

gaps.gap: The flight result is a static cross-section standing in for a dynamic claim. Every anchor work carries the abandonment half as a within-item, over-time statement (Berger & Le Mens's rise-rate → decline-rate; Lieberson's per-name lead-lag); S10 has a single Spearman between a word's pooled lift and one group's current relative use, which is compatible with a stable stratification that never cycles.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: A member fixed-effects event study at the word level: for each of the ~40–119 style words that clear the volume thresholds, estimate a takeoff year from the pooled series, then regress each member's rate of THAT word on event time (pre/post takeoff) with member fixed effects, interacted with status tier. The cycle predicts the status-top's within-member slope turns negative after takeoff while the bottom tier's turns positive; a stable stratification predicts both slopes flat. Report the tier×post interaction, not the level difference.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data. provinces/segments_*.jsonl already carries speaker, province, date and text; build_class_word_year.py aggregates to class|year and would need only the member key retained to produce member × word × year counts. member_year_rates.json and member_word_vectors.json show the member-level plumbing already exists.

gaps.gap: The flight statistic is mathematically coupled: flight_correlation.py computes lift from the ALL-CLASS pooled corpus — which contains class II — and then correlates it with the class I / class II ratio. Words whose rise was driven by class II are mechanically both high-lift and low-I/II, so a negative rho is the expected value under no status behaviour at all. This is Pearson's shared-denominator problem plus regression to the mean in a ratio of noisy rates, and it explains the sign, not merely the precision.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Three fixes, all cheap: (a) leave-out lift — recompute lift from the corpus EXCLUDING classes I and II (or excluding the comparison group in each ladder run), so the change score and the ratio share no counts; (b) split-half — lift estimated on odd-indexed members, the ratio on even-indexed; (c) a null distribution for rho generated by permuting class labels across members while holding each member's text fixed, reported at every volume threshold. If the headline −0.42 survives (a) and sits outside (c), the result is real; if it attenuates toward the permutation mean, it was coupling.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data. ~30 lines of edits to flight_correlation.py, flight_ladders.py and build_class_word_year.py; runs in minutes.

gaps.gap: No drift null. The cultural-evolution branch of this literature (Bentley et al. 2004; Acerbi & Bentley 2014; Newberry et al. 2017) treats unbiased copying as the null that a fashion-cycle claim must beat, because random drift alone produces turnover, rise/fall asymmetry, and apparent group differences at finite sample sizes. S10 reports no neutral baseline anywhere in the chase-and-flight family.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Simulate unbiased copying over the style-word set at the observed per-class-year token totals and initial frequencies; report the sampling distribution of the flight rho at each volume threshold, of the class-gap trend, and of the peak-migration statistic under neutrality. Optionally apply the Frequency Increment Test per word to the class-resolved series to separate selection from drift, with the Karjus et al. binning caveat handled by reporting across bin widths.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data — class_word_year.json plus the token totals it already stores are the only inputs the simulation needs.

gaps.gap: Word-level inference treats words as independent observations. p = 0.004 at n = 40 assumes 40 exchangeable units, but the named examples include a morphological pair (advocating/advocates), and style-word frequencies co-vary through topic and collocation. The study's own record notes it has been bitten three times by unclustered SEs; this is the same wound on the flight battery.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Collapse to lemma families before ranking; block-bootstrap over MEMBERS (not words) to get the rho CI; and report a single family-wise permutation p across the whole 5-ladder × 4-threshold grid by permuting member-to-group assignment, which preserves inter-word correlation exactly. Report the family as one number, since the draft already concedes the runs are not independent.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data; the permutation needs member-resolved counts, i.e. the same rebuild as gap 1.

gaps.gap: The 'peak does not migrate' finding is adjudicated by an aggregation choice, and the draft says so: member-year aggregation WOULD show the peak migrating downward, and this is dismissed as an artifact of long-serving members. To a sociolinguist that difference is not an artifact to be weighted away — it is precisely the Sankoff–Blondeau decomposition of community change into within-individual change versus cohort replacement, and the cycle's central prediction is currently resting on which of the two you happen to compute.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Run both and report both, decomposed: (i) within-member change in register rate across the six bins for members present in ≥2 bins (the panel component), (ii) between-cohort differences among entering members (the replacement component), each by class tier. A class × era APC model is the compact form; apc_chamber_decomposition.py already implements the machinery for chambers and can be pointed at the class panel. The claim to defend is then 'the peak is static once lifespan change is separated from cohort replacement', which is a real claim; the current one is a weighting artefact in either direction.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data (member-year panel rates already exist in member_year_rates.json / fpw_member_year.json).

gaps.gap: No lead-lag: the direction of diffusion is never demonstrated. Lieberson's claim is credible because names are shown to appear at the top FIRST and below LATER, name by name. S10's own text concedes the era test cannot say who originated the form and that class coding only becomes substantial around 2005 — so 'chase' and 'flight' are labels attached to a cross-sectional gradient, and the same gradient is produced by any stable difference in adoption rate with no cycle.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Per-word takeoff-year estimation by tier: fit a logistic/S-curve (or a simple threshold-crossing date) to each style word's rate series separately within each class or ladder tier, then test whether the top tier's crossing date systematically precedes the bottom tier's across words (a paired sign/Wilcoxon test over words). This is the analysis that converts the correlation into a diffusion claim. For words that took off before ~2005 the class coding is too thin, so report it on post-2005 takeoffs and state the restriction.
gaps.feasibility: Mostly computable from held data for post-2005 takeoffs. Establishing the ORIGIN of the 1994–96 turn needs new collection — class-coded Commons speech 1985–96, which §8.6 already names.

gaps.gap: No evaluation evidence. Labov and Trudgill both establish that the variable carries social meaning for the speakers before reading production differences as status behaviour; S10 has production only, so 'the top avoids the words that became common' has no evidence separating status-avoidance from role, portfolio, or drafting-practice differences.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Either (a) a subjective-reaction/matched-guise rating study: pairs of legislative excerpts differing only in register-word density, rated by lay or practitioner panels on competence/authenticity/'sounds machine-written' — the direct analogue of Labov's test; or (b) a corpus proxy: occurrences within the record itself of members commenting on machine-drafted or formulaic speech (heckles, points of order, press coverage), showing the marker is socially noticed and by whom.
gaps.feasibility: (a) needs new collection — a rating study, modest but genuinely new. (b) is computable from held data by keyword-searching the 22-chamber corpus for metalinguistic commentary, and would be a cheap partial answer.

gaps.gap: Topic confound uncontrolled. Class II is teachers, nurses, social workers and journalists; the words that rose (primary, advocating, advocates, outcomes) are plausibly the vocabulary of the portfolios those members speak on. Rate-per-1,000-words cannot distinguish 'class I avoids status-contaminated markers' from 'class I speaks about different bills'.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Residualise word rates on debate topic before computing lift and relative use — either by restricting the comparison to speaker pairs within the same debate/bill (the strongest version: a within-debate fixed effect on the flight correlation), or by topic-modelling the segments and partialling topic loadings out. If the flight rho survives within-debate, the topic objection is dead; if it vanishes, the claim was portfolio composition.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data — segments carry debate-level metadata; a within-debate restriction needs no modelling at all, only a grouping key.

gaps.gap: Rate-per-word rather than rate-per-opportunity violates the accountability principle, which is the first thing a variationist referee checks. The 407-word Kobak ruler is a bag of markers, not a set of alternants for a single meaning, so no envelope of variation is defined.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Use the held open-model log-probs to build an opportunity-normalised measure: at each token position, the model's distribution over alternatives gives the probability mass the style word displaced, so the measure becomes 'chose the marker when a marker slot was available'. Even a coarse surprisal-normalised rate would let the paper say the effect is not frequency-of-topic. Report the flight correlation on both the raw and the opportunity-normalised rate.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data (log-probs from open models are already in hand), but this is the most compute-hungry item on the list — a re-scoring pass over the provincial scan.

gaps.gap: The compression trend (t = −1.67 over six five-year bins) is reported as 'short of significance' with no power statement and no binning robustness, and Karjus et al. 2020 exists precisely because corpus-change results move with binning choices. As written, a referee cannot tell whether compression is absent or undetectable.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: State the minimum detectable slope at the observed SEs, and re-run the class-gap trend across bin widths (3/4/5/7-year), across anchor points (data-end vs data-start), and with member-level bootstrap CIs rather than inverse-variance weights alone. Report the envelope, not one binning.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data; class_gap_trend.py and build_class_by_era.py already produce everything needed.

gaps.gap: The abstention result (free work flat at every threshold) is an unrejected null presented as a confirmed third pattern of the geometry. The field will not accept a non-significant coefficient as evidence of indifference.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Equivalence testing (TOST) on the free-work rho at each threshold, with the equivalence bound set to the smallest rho the chase/flight tiers exhibit (≈0.15–0.19), so the paper can say 'the off-ladder group's response is bounded below the weakest on-ladder response' rather than 'flat'.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data; a few lines on the existing flight_ladders.py output.

gaps.gap: No out-of-sample replication. The whole chase-and-flight battery runs on one provincial scan and re-slices the same corpus five ways; the anchor works replicate in a separately collected community (NYC→Philadelphia, France→US). The draft correctly calls the five ladders a robustness family rather than replications, which leaves the claim with zero replications.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Pre-specify the flight test and run it once on the 17 non-Canadian chambers using status markers that need no new coding: Wikipedia-article-length quintiles (already at 99% coverage over 6,896 members across all 22 chambers) and office-holder versus backbencher. Both already show top-retreat in the level analysis, so the flight prediction on them is a genuine out-of-sample test with a pre-registered direction.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data — no new collection; the prominence and office codings already span all 22 chambers. Extending the CLASS coding beyond Canada would need new occupational collection, but the test does not require it.

gaps.gap: Word-set fragility. The headline rho rests on 40 words at the 800+ threshold and −0.46 on 25 words at 1,500+, with four named exemplars carrying the interpretation; no influence diagnostics are reported.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Leave-one-word-out and leave-one-lemma-family-out jackknife on rho at each threshold; report the largest single-word influence (likely `primary`, at 2.35× lift) and the full threshold curve with bootstrap bands rather than four point estimates.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data; minutes.

gaps.gap: No style/monitoring stratification of the flight effect, which is the dimension Labov's crossover is actually defined on — the crossover appears in the MOST monitored styles. S10 already measures scriptedness and genre for the prevalence arm but does not cross it with the status batteries.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Run the flight correlation separately within scripted and unscripted genres. A status-display mechanism predicts flight is strongest in the most prepared, most monitored speech; a drafting-practice mechanism predicts the opposite. This is a cheap discriminating test and it maps S10's design onto Labov's original axis, which is rhetorically valuable given the paper leans on him.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from held data — the genre/scriptedness labels used in the prevalence analysis apply to the same segments.

surveys.verdict: S10 falls short of the field's standard for a fashion-cycle claim — every nearest work carries either individual-level adoption/abandonment trajectories, item-by-item lead-lag, or an explicit drift null, and S10 has none of the three, while its headline flight statistic is additionally exposed to a shared-denominator artifact that predicts the observed sign under no status behaviour at all — but its 30-year member-resolved real-time record exceeds what Labov, Lieberson and Berger had, so the two decisive analyses (a within-member event study around each word's takeoff, and a neutral-copying null) are computable from data already in hand; the hypothesis-not-finding framing is currently the correct call and does not have to remain one.

nearest_works.work: Ethan Fosse & Christopher Winship, "Bounding Analyses of Age-Period-Cohort Effects"
nearest_works.venue_year: Demography 56(5): 1975-2004, 2019 (companion review: Fosse & Winship, Annual Review of Sociology 45: 467-492, 2019)
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: That credible APC claims are possible without point identification: one can partially identify the relative sizes of age, period and cohort linear effects from theory-driven inequality constraints.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: Algebraic decomposition separating what the data identify with no assumptions (all nonlinearities / second differences, plus the one-parameter 'canonical solution line' of linear slopes) from what they never identify (the individual slopes); demonstration that every constraint-based estimator silently selects one point on that line with identical model fit; translation of substantive theory into sign, monotonicity and relative-magnitude constraints; results reported as intervals (bounds), not point estimates; worked empirical example showing when bounds are informative and when they are vacuous.

nearest_works.work: Ohjae Gowen, Ethan Fosse & Christopher Winship, "Cross-Group Differences in Age, Period, and Cohort Effects: A Bounding Approach to the Gender Wage Gap"
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: That cohort (not period or age) drives the change in a between-group gap — i.e. exactly S10's move of identifying APC components from divergent group histories.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: A cross-strata linearized APC (CSL-APC) re-parameterization whose first result is negative and load-bearing: differencing across groups does NOT identify the linear cross-group APC effects. Point identification requires an explicit equality-of-effects assumption (one scale's effect equal across groups), defended on two grounds — substantive theory AND a testable implication, that the group-differenced NONLINEAR effects of that scale are ~0, checked with joint F-tests and AIC/BIC comparisons of models dropping each nonlinearity block (in their case the test failed, so they fell back to bounds). Bounds derived from monotonicity assumptions over stated age/period ranges, plus two sensitivity analyses: whether an assumption set is internally consistent, and whether the binding constraint hinges on a single extreme nonlinear estimate.

nearest_works.work: Andrew Bell, "Age period cohort analysis: a review of what we should and shouldn't do"
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: A prescriptive standard: no mechanical solution to the identification problem exists; cohort claims are credible only when the identifying assumption is stated, strong and theory-based.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: Review + demonstration that identification bites only on linear components (so nonlinearities are free); worked example that the same data plotted two ways implies opposite APC readings; a graded menu of legitimate strategies — fix one slope at a stated value, impose inequality/sign constraints (citing Fosse-Winship bounding), or use mechanism-based modelling (Winship & Harding 2008) that substitutes a measured mechanism variable for one time scale; and an explicit blacklist: HAPC, the intrinsic estimator and PLS are said to hide their constraints, with HAPC in particular usually behaving as though it assumes no linear cohort effect (Bell & Jones 2014a, 2014c, 2018; Luo & Hodges 2016, 2019).

nearest_works.work: Liying Luo & John Robert Warren, "Describing and explaining age, period, and cohort trends in Americans' vocabulary knowledge"
nearest_works.venue_year: Population Research and Policy Review 42:26, 2023 (method: Luo & Hodges, Sociological Methods & Research 51(3): 1164-1210, 2022)
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: That specific birth cohorts (1940-54 high, 1965+ low) differ in a language outcome (GSS WORDSUM) net of age and period, and that education largely explains the earlier cohorts' advantage.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: APC-I model, in which cohort effects are age-by-period interactions so INTER-COHORT DEVIATIONS from the additive baseline are identified without any constraint; a global F-test that cohort deviations exist at all before interpreting any single cohort; per-cohort t-tests of deviation with effect sizes; intra-cohort life-course slopes testing whether cohort gaps persist or converge as cohorts age; progressive mediation models (education, newspaper reading, TV) to convert a cohort label into a mechanism; stratified robustness by item type (basic vs advanced, obsolete vs non-obsolete words); and an appendix showing that HAPC results on the same data flip with the random-effects specification.

nearest_works.work: Gaurav Kamath, Michelle Yang, Siva Reddy, Morgan Sonderegger & Dallas Card, "Semantic change in adults is not primarily a generational phenomenon"
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: The direct competitor claim, in S10's own data type: in US congressional speech, language change is NOT primarily generational — older members adopt new usage within a few years.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: 7.9M speeches, 1873-2010, ~1.5B words, speaker birth dates joined from an external legislator roster; procedural speech removed with a trained classifier; GAMMs with speaker random effects and a single theory-motivated age-offset parameter alpha (a time-shift parameterization that states its assumption — change is a function of time, or time and age, but not age alone — rather than trying to free-estimate all three scales); an unconstrained GAMM (arbitrary joint function of time, age and their interaction) fitted as a check, showing near-identical fit so the constraint is not manufacturing the answer; Bayesian meta-analysis over 163 senses of 81 words giving alpha = 0.13 [0.10, 0.16]; individual speakers' trajectories showing within-lifetime change; word-sense induction manually audited with artifact senses dropped. Headline reported in interpretable units: a 20-year age gap = ~3 years of lag.

nearest_works.work: Gillian Sankoff & Hélène Blondeau, "Language change across the lifespan: /r/ in Montreal French"
nearest_works.venue_year: Language 83(3): 560-588, 2007 (with the apparent-time baseline: Bailey, Wikle, Tillery & Sand, Language Variation and Change 3: 241-264, 1991)
nearest_works.what_they_claimed: That an apparent-time (birth-cohort) gradient is largely but not wholly valid evidence of generational change, because some adults change in the middle of the observation window.
nearest_works.evidence_they_marshalled: Real-time panel: the same speakers from the 1971 Montreal corpus re-recorded 13 years later, set against the community trend sample from the same speech community; per-speaker classification into stable vs changed trajectories; explicit reconciliation of the apparent-time slope against the observed lifespan movement. The field convention this set: a cohort/generational claim must exhibit trend evidence AND panel evidence and must state which part of the apparent-time gradient survives once adult change is deducted.
