field_standard: Write the identification problem in equations, and name exactly which linear combinations the design identifies (here: age+period, and cohort-age) — prose acknowledgement is no longer sufficient.
Publish the canonical solution line: the full one-parameter family of (age, period, cohort) slopes that fit identically, so the reported number is visibly one point on it rather than an estimate.
Lead with the quantities that are identified without assumptions — nonlinear cohort deviations / second differences — and treat any linear slope as a derived, assumption-contingent object.
Turn the substantive story into explicit sign, monotonicity or magnitude constraints on at least one scale, and report the resulting BOUNDS as the headline estimate.

Where the identifying assumption has a testable implication (e.g. equality of a scale's effect across groups implies group-differenced nonlinearities ~ 0), test it: joint F-test plus model-fit comparison, and report the failure if it fails.
Run sensitivity analyses on the assumption set itself: internal consistency, and whether a binding constraint rests on one noisy cell.
Prefer mechanism-based identification — replace one time scale with a measured mechanism variable and show it carries the effect (Winship-Harding, endorsed by both Bell and Fosse-Winship).
Rule out age-grading / life-cycle explicitly with panel evidence on the same individuals, and report intra-cohort dynamics: do cohort gaps persist, widen, or converge as cohorts age?
Show the data grid (Lexis-style birth x period cell counts) and demonstrate the slope is not carried by sparse corner cells; leave-one-cell and leave-one-population-out re-estimates.
Do not present HAPC or intrinsic-estimator output as a solution; if referees ask for it, name the hidden constraint it imposes and show the sensitivity.
Report the effect in interpretable units and against a published benchmark from the same kind of data (e.g. years of drift per decade of birth).
Cluster inference at the level of the identifying variation — individual AND group — with small-G corrections (wild cluster bootstrap, randomization inference) when the group count is small.
Replicate across independent populations, and test cross-population heterogeneity formally (interaction or random-slope variance), not by comparing ranges of interval estimates.
Placebo the outcome instrument itself, so the cohort gradient cannot be the measure tracking cohort differences in topic or role rather than the construct.
we_meet: Item 1 (name the identified combinations): §4.6 states that birth+period and age+period fits reproduce each other exactly and that only (age+period) and (cohort-age) are identified — this is Bell's core demand and most applied papers fail it.

Item 8, half (panel evidence exists): the member-fixed-effects estimate of +0.51 per 1,000 words per decade over 8,600 members with 3+ years is precisely the real-time/panel component Sankoff-Blondeau and Kamath treat as mandatory; almost no APC paper in demography has individual panel data at all.

Item 13, partially (multi-population replication): 22 chambers, 5 countries, 61,312 member-years, 7,027 members — broader than Rekker's 21-country APC vote-choice design and far broader than any single-survey APC paper.

Item 12, partially (clustering): member-clustered SEs and member-cluster bootstrap CIs throughout, with Appendix A item 3 documenting the unclustered-inference failure mode and correcting it (t 17.7 -> 8-9) rather than hiding it.

An explicit pre-treatment placebo cell: the US Senate gradient among cohorts born 1917-1964 observed 1994-2004, +105 [+47, +155] per 100k per decade — a genuine 'the gradient predates the treatment' demonstration that the nearest published works do not have an analogue of.

Item 14, partially (selection story tested the right way round): occupation and education controls STRENGTHEN the birth term (+1.05 -> +1.14), reported as running against a composition/selection explanation.
One mechanism candidate excluded on data rather than assertion: ministerial office (Appendix D.4), where the gradient strengthens once office years are removed.

A second, non-collinear clock is already computed: entry year in cohort_vs_period.py with a documented left-censoring rule — the raw material for the discriminating test the field wants (see gap on tenure).

The group-vs-individual figure (apc_gradients.png) is an informal version of the cross-strata homogeneity argument Gowen-Fosse-Winship make formally: divergent chamber trends (-173 to +413) against a tight within-year birth gradient (+49 to +109).

gaps.gap: The headline number is the least-identified object in the model, presented as an estimate. +0.88/decade is one point on a line; the field has required the whole line since Fosse-Winship 2019.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Publish the canonical solution line for the two-stamp fit as a table/figure: from b_year = a+p = 1.25 and b_birth = c-a = 0.88, report p = 1.25-a and c = 0.88+a across the plausible range of the age slope a. Then bound it: under the juniority sign assumption (a <= 0), +0.88 is an UPPER bound on the cohort slope, and a lower bound follows from capping |a|. The cap is already in the study — the pre-drift US Senate cell (cohorts born 1917-1964, all formed before any drift, so c ~ 0 there) estimates a ~ -1.05 per decade directly. Propagate that through c = b_birth + a per chamber-era to produce bounded cohort slopes. Requires putting the /1,000-word and /100k-word rulers on one scale first.
gaps.feasibility: Arithmetic on coefficients already estimated; no new data, no new fits. Half a day.

gaps.gap: No analysis of the quantities that are identified with no assumptions at all. The cohort claim rests entirely on a linear slope while the free lunch — inter-cohort deviations from the additive age-by-period baseline — is untouched. This is the single item that would let S10 state a cohort result no APC critic can strike out.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Fit the APC-I model (Luo & Hodges, SMR 2022; APCI package in R/Stata) on member-year cells: global F-test for the age-by-period interaction block first, then per-cohort deviation estimates with t-tests — especially for the post-1985 'drift-formed' cohorts the steepening claim rests on — then intra-cohort slopes testing whether each cohort's deviation persists or fades as it ages. A localized deviation at specific birth years is far stronger evidence than any linear slope.
gaps.feasibility: Fully computable from data in hand (member-year rate, birth year, spoken year, chamber). Days, not weeks; sits on top of cohort_vs_period.py.

gaps.gap: The stated identification strategy — 'identified via cross-legislature divergent group histories' — is asserted rather than implemented, and the nearest formal treatment says it does not work on its own. Gowen-Fosse-Winship 2023 prove that cross-group differencing leaves the linear cross-group APC effects unidentified; it buys identification only under an explicit equality-of-effects assumption.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: (a) State the assumption in the paper's own terms (the within-year birth/age profile is common across chambers and era-stable). (b) Test its testable implication the way GFW do: compare the NONLINEAR birth-deviation profiles across chambers and across eras — joint F-test plus AIC/BIC on models dropping each cross-chamber nonlinearity block — instead of arguing from the +49 to +109 range of point estimates. (c) Replace the range argument with a formal heterogeneity test: chamber-by-birth interaction, or a random-slope variance component with its CI.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from the five chambers with exact birth years, but G = 5 is small: needs wild cluster bootstrap or randomization inference at the chamber level, not member-only bootstrap.

gaps.gap: Age-grading by career stage is the live rival, and the test that discriminates it is buried in a footnote and dismissed as 're-description'. Tenure (year - entry) is NOT collinear with the APC triple because entry age varies across members; it is the one extra clock the data contain, and referees will treat 'juniority' as a career-stage claim until it is tested.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Run the fully-conditioned cell regression: within (birth year x spoken year x chamber) cells, regress the register rate on tenure. That estimate is net of age, period AND cohort simultaneously — it is the clean test of whether the gradient is about being new to the chamber (scripted maiden/prepared statements, staff-drafted set-pieces) or about birth cohort. Promote the three-stamp decomposition (birth +0.69 with entry year in) from footnote r46a to a result, with the entry-cohort vs birth-cohort split reported as the finding.
gaps.feasibility: Data in hand — cohort_vs_period.py already loads entry year with a documented left-censoring rule; the cost is the censored rows (37,548 of 61,312) and thinner cells.

gaps.gap: No mechanism-based identification, which is the exit both Bell (2020) and Fosse-Winship endorse and which S10's own theory names: formation in the ambient written culture. As written, 'cohort' is a clock, not a cause.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Build an ambient-register exposure index: score the same instrument word list against an external, era-spanning corpus (Google Books n-grams, COHA, or a newspaper archive) to get its yearly rate back to ~1900, then assign each member the mean level over their formation window (e.g. ages 15-25). Substitute that index for birth year in the two-stamp fit. If it absorbs the birth term, the cohort effect is identified through a measured mechanism rather than a clock, and the claimed shape (flat for pre-drift cohorts, steepening after) becomes a fitted prediction rather than an assumption. A null here is publishable and honest — and note the three failed exposure tests in Appendix A were technology-adoption and province measures, not ambient text.
gaps.feasibility: Needs new collection, but cheap and public: Google Books n-grams give yearly frequencies for the instrument's words back a century, and formation_window.py already exists. Weeks.

gaps.gap: The nearest published work in the same data type reaches the opposite conclusion and is not engaged. Kamath et al. (PNAS 2025) fit speaker age against calendar time on US congressional speech and report alpha = 0.13 [0.10, 0.16] — 'not primarily a generational phenomenon'.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Cite it, and translate S10's gradient into their units: alpha = b_birth / b_year = 0.88 / 1.25 ~ 0.70, i.e. a decade of birth is worth ~7 years of calendar drift, roughly 5x their age effect. State why register might behave differently from word sense (register is a socialized production norm acquired in a formation window; word sense is comprehension-driven and adopted on contact). Also copy their key robustness move: fit an unconstrained model (register as an arbitrary joint function of year, age and their interaction) and show it does not beat the constrained parameterization on fit — this is what stops a referee saying the constraint made the result.
gaps.feasibility: The units translation is arithmetic; the unconstrained-vs-constrained fit comparison is modest new code (GAM or spline tensor on member-years). Days.

gaps.gap: The panel is not used for the test sociolinguistics actually accepts — convergence vs parallel gaps — and the informal 40% split is not a decomposition. Worse, the between-member (+1.25) and within-member (+0.51) estimates target the SAME identified quantity (age+period) and disagree by a factor of 2.4; under a homogeneous linear APC model they should not.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: (a) Estimate within-member slopes BY birth cohort and plot the cohort gaps at successive periods: converging gaps = period/zeitgeist, persistent or widening gaps = cohort. (b) Replace 'roughly 40% happens inside careers' with a Firebaugh cohort-replacement decomposition (Sociological Methodology 19: 243-262, 1989) with standard errors, per chamber. (c) Reconcile the 1.25 vs 0.51 discrepancy explicitly — heterogeneous slopes, nonlinearity, or entry/exit correlated with the outcome — since a referee will read it as evidence of specification failure.
gaps.feasibility: Entirely in hand: 8,600 members with 3+ years, member-year panel already assembled.

gaps.gap: The 'steepening' half of the claim — the load-bearing half, since it is what ties the gradient to drift-formed cohorts — is read off two overlapping-or-not confidence intervals per chamber, with no single test statistic and no multiplicity control. The US House pre-era interval already includes zero (+23 [-22, +64]).
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: An explicit triple-interaction estimate (birth gradient x era x chamber) with one coefficient, one CI, a pre-specified era boundary, and a correction across the chambers and era splits examined; plus a specification curve over the reasonable lattice (era boundary, min-word threshold, weighting, cohort binning) — infrastructure the study already uses elsewhere.
gaps.feasibility: Computable from apc_chamber_decomposition.py outputs; the pre-specification point can only be handled honestly by labelling it exploratory if it was not registered.

gaps.gap: The instrument has no placebo in the cohort analysis. Cohorts differ in portfolio, committee and role, so a frequency-matched word list could reproduce a birth gradient from topic composition alone. S10 built exactly this null for the trend work and did not carry it across.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Re-estimate the two-stamp birth coefficient against each of the existing frequency- and dispersion-matched placebo word sets (200 in the class work, 1,000 in the New Brunswick ITS), and report the instrument's percentile in that empirical null. Add a topic-matched null (matched on frequency AND semantic field) if the plain frequency match also fires.
gaps.feasibility: Entirely in hand — in_time_placebo.py and fig_trend.py already build and score the placebo sets.

gaps.gap: No data grid. Linear APC slopes are notoriously driven by sparse corner cells (very young members in the 1990s, very old members in the 2020s), and Bell's central pedagogical point is that how you display the grid encodes the assumption.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: A Lexis-style table/figure of birth-decade x spoken-year cells with member and word counts; a support-trimmed re-estimate dropping cells below a stated count; leave-one-chamber-out and leave-one-cell-out slopes.
gaps.feasibility: In hand; hours.

gaps.gap: HAPC will be requested by referees from the Yang-Land tradition, and the study has no stated position on it.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: One paragraph declining HAPC-CCREM with the citations (Bell & Jones 2014a 'Another futile quest?', 2014c 'Don't birth cohorts matter?'; Luo & Hodges 2016, 2019 — HAPC behaves as though it assumes no linear cohort effect), optionally fitting it once as a sensitivity with the hidden constraint named. Note that Luo & Warren's own appendix shows HAPC results on a language outcome flip with the random-effects specification.
gaps.feasibility: Prose plus an optional short fit; in hand.

gaps.gap: Measurement invariance of the transcript across chambers and eras is untested for this claim. Hansard-style editing conventions differ and have changed; if reporters standardize senior members' speech differently, part of a 'juniority' gradient is a reporting artifact.
gaps.data_or_analysis_needed: Split the gradient by chambers with verbatim vs edited transcription policy (the 22-chamber policy scan already collected the policies); and, as an external check, re-estimate the gradient on a written stream where transcription does not intervene (parliamentary motions/written questions — the Suvanto et al. comparator).
gaps.feasibility: The chamber split is in hand; the written-motion stream needs new collection.

surveys.verdict: S10 exceeds the field on raw evidentiary breadth — 22 chambers, an individual panel, a genuine pre-treatment placebo cell, and an honest statement of which combinations are identified — but falls short of the post-2019 APC standard on the part that decides the claim: it headlines an unidentified linear slope with no canonical solution line, no bounds, no analysis of the identified nonlinear cohort deviations, no formal test of the cross-legislature homogeneity assumption it identifies off, and no test of the tenure/age-grading rival it already holds the data to run — and every one of those except the ambient-exposure mechanism index is computable from data already in hand.

# S10 Evidence-Standards Synthesis
### Cross-claim reading of seven adjacent-literature surveys — 2026-08-26

---

## 1. Per-claim verdicts

| Claim | One-line verdict | Worst gap severity | Gap counts (blocking / expected / nice) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **new-sociometric-measure** | Ahead of every comparator on preregistration, blinding and cross-population replication; missing nearly the whole classical construct-validation core, so the evidence supports "a useful occupational index built for this study," not "a new measure of socioeconomic position." | **blocking** | 5 / 7 / 2 |
| **prevalence** | The best-calibrated detector-based prevalence estimate in this literature on specificity, bias direction and corpus hygiene — but missing the three exhibits the strongest works are built on: known-α recovery, a time series with a flat pre-ChatGPT segment, and calibration of the Mixed fraction the 9.03% headline actually rests on. | **blocking** | 3 / 7 / 4 |
| **register-predates-models** | Instrument design (ruler fixed independently of the years measured, matched placebos) exceeds the field; the headline sentence claims more chambers and more decades than the §4.5a tables support, and the marker list was selected on the very outcome the backward projection claims to find. | **blocking** | 3 / 8 / 3 |
| **post-training-artifact** | Estimator hygiene above the field median; the attribution half of the checklist is entirely absent, so the sentence as written (an *objective* claim) overshoots a design that can only support a *data* claim. | **blocking** | 2 / 4 / 3 |
| **quality-null** | The direction of the finding is well supported and honestly caveated; the "+0.29 sd" figure is not referee-proof — no human gold standard, no label-error correction, and no test that the detector selects on form. | **blocking** | 3 / 6 / 2 |
| **detector-evasion** | The narrow claim ("a directed blind search walked ~1 in 5 flagged Pangram-4 speeches to Human") is over-evidenced by field norms; the general claim ("detection is not a security control") is under-evidenced — one detector, one attacker, detector-label ground truth, and a vendor-vs-us "10×". | **blocking** | 3 / 8 / 3 |
| **permeation** | Inference hygiene and source-side provenance exceed every comparator; identification does not — no control words, no separation of within-member drift from turnover, no spontaneity guarantee, so a competent referee reads +0.01 as an unidentified corpus-composition effect. | **blocking** | 3 / 8 / 1 |
| **chase-and-flight** | Weakest arm. The headline flight statistic is mathematically coupled such that its observed sign is the expected value under no status behaviour at all; the cycle claim has none of the three things every comparator carries. Correctly framed as hypothesis-not-finding, and the decisive fixes are in hand. | **blocking** | 4 / 8 / 2 |

**Totals: 26 blocking, 56 expected-by-reviewers, 20 nice-to-have.** Of the 26 blocking gaps, **24 are closable from artifacts already committed in `analysis/s10/` plus compute, API spend, or public data.** Only two are not: the human-coded DQI gold standard (quality-null gaps 1–2), which no reanalysis substitutes for. The "folk ladder" blocking gap is closable by a free text edit (rename) or by new rater collection, at Matthew's choice.

---

## 2. Top 10 recommendations, ranked by leverage per effort

**1. De-couple the flight correlation and give it a permutation null.**
`flight_correlation.py` computes each word's lift from the all-class pooled corpus (which contains class II) and then correlates it with the class I / class II ratio. Words whose rise was driven by class II are mechanically both high-lift and low-I/II, so **a negative ρ is the null expectation with no status behaviour whatever**. Fix three ways: (a) leave-out lift computed excluding the comparison classes; (b) split-half — lift on odd-indexed members, ratio on even; (c) a null distribution from permuting class labels across members with text held fixed, at every volume threshold.
*Claims:* chase-and-flight (blocking). *Data:* held only. *Effort:* ~30 lines against `flight_correlation.py` / `flight_ladders.py` / `build_class_word_year.py`; runs in minutes.
*Why first:* it is the cheapest analysis in the report and the only one that can turn a stated headline into an artifact. Run it before the section is defended, not after.

**2. Score the preference data itself, plus a length control and a base-prompting arm.**
Three cheap moves that together convert the post-training arm from descriptive to attributive. (a) Compute register excess on chosen-vs-rejected pairs in the public Tulu-3 preference mixture — paired within-pair difference with bootstrap CI, win-rate of the higher-register member, both length-residualised. This is the move both nearest neighbours (Sharma ICLR 2024; Juzek & Ward) treat as decisive, and it needs no checkpoint downloads. (b) Truncate every generation to the shortest common length within its prompt pair and re-run all stage deltas; also regress per-prompt register excess on stage with log(tokens). (c) A URIAL-style four-arm test (base raw / base with 3-shot stylistic prefix / instruct with template / instruct without) reporting what share of the +1.24 each arm recovers.
*Claims:* post-training-artifact (1 blocking dented, 3 expected closed). *Data:* public preference mixture + generations already held. *Effort:* (a) hours, (b) an afternoon, (c) inference only on models already run.

**3. The zero-cost bundle from committed artifacts.** Seven re-analyses that need no new data of any kind:
- Split the prevalence headline and every chamber rate by 2025 vs 2026 with CIs and name which estimand 9.03% is (pooled flag rate is 10.15% in 2025 vs 15.79% in 2026, z≈4.1) — *prevalence, dents a blocking gap.*
- Re-run the prevalence ratio bootstrap resampling **speakers** within chamber; report the design effect (`speaker` is already a column in `pangram_p4_verdicts.csv`) — *prevalence, expected.*
- Beta-binomial / logit-normal random-effects fit across chambers; report τ, I² (≈0.81 on committed verdicts), and empirical-Bayes shrunken rates beside the raw 11× — *prevalence, expected.*
- Threshold/operating curves off the continuous `fraction_ai`: prevalence-vs-cutoff against the FPR each cutoff buys on the 1,260 controls; the same sweep for the evasion arm, which simultaneously supplies the field-required defense/recalibration element — *prevalence + detector-evasion, expected.*
- Polychoric correlation matrix and one-factor graded-response IRT on the committed `stage1/2_grades_by_id.json`; re-run the AI–human contrast on the latent score — *quality-null, expected.*
- TOST equivalence tests against a pre-specified SESOI: quality's three null dimensions and the 63 evasion pairs; and the free-work abstention ρ against the weakest on-ladder ρ (≈0.15) — *quality-null + chase-and-flight, expected.*
- Rename the folk ladder ("model-elicited element weighting" / "stereotype-composed ladder") and delete every sentence implying a population holds the image — *new-sociometric-measure, closes a blocking gap for free.*
*Data:* held only. *Effort:* 1–2 days for all seven.

## 3. Cross-claim patterns

**P1 — Six of the seven claims are single-instrument, and every adjacent field requires two.** One ruler, one detector, one judge, one attacker, one model family, one word list. The two arms that already carry a second instrument (permeation's two scorer families; prevalence's Opus screen plus two reported-though-disagreeing zero-shot detectors) are the arms whose surveys read most favourably. Recommendation 4 is the single structural fix; it touches three claims.

**P2 — The same missing object recurs in four arms: a control that shares the instrument's construction but not its content.** Permeation has no control word set at all; register-predates has 200 placebos matched on frequency and dispersion but not on pre-period trend, which is precisely the dimension the endogeneity objection runs through; cohort-juniority never applies the placebo sets that exist elsewhere in the study; chase-and-flight has no unbiased-copying null. One donor-set generator answers all four (Recommendation 7).

**P3 — Aggregate-versus-individual decomposition is the standard demand in every arm with a time dimension, and S10 has already done it once, correctly.** §4.6's within-member fixed-effects drift is exactly the Sankoff–Blondeau real-time/panel decomposition the field requires, complete with the retraction of the earlier underpowered null. It is not ported to permeation (where turnover is the leading rival, made so by S10's own birth-year finding), to chase-and-flight (where the peak-migration result is currently adjudicated by which aggregation you happen to compute — that difference is not an artifact to weight away, it *is* the decomposition), or to the convergence-versus-parallel-gaps test in cohort-juniority. One workstream, four gaps, three of them blocking.

**P4 — Genre and scriptedness composition is the unmeasured confound behind four claims simultaneously.** S10's own §4.3 finding (3.29× gradient, SO31 vs Oral Questions) makes genre-mix drift a first-order threat anywhere a rate is compared across time, chamber, class or verdict — and genre labels exist for one of 22 chambers. This is the highest-value single asset the study does not have.

**P5 — Selection on the instrument appears in three arms in the same shape.** The marker list was selected on the post-2022 jump and then run backwards (register-predates); the treatment variable is a detector verdict and the outcome is textual form, which detectors key on (quality-null); the headline weight is a continuous vendor output on segments selected by that same vendor's flag (prevalence). Each has the same fix — run the selection rule on text where the true effect is zero by construction. S10 has already invented this move twice (the in-time placebo, the 1,260 pre-2022 controls); it just has not pointed it at these three.

**P6 — Ground truth is missing in three arms where it could be manufactured cheaply.** Prevalence and evasion both use a detector verdict as truth when synthesised text with known machine fraction costs a few thousand API calls; quality uses an LLM judge as truth when 150 human codes would anchor it. Three arms currently validate against themselves, and two of the three could stop doing so this month.

**P7 — Effect stability is repeatedly offered where measurement invariance is required.** 21-of-22 chambers with the same sign (new-measure), 22 chambers and three decades (register-predates), sign agreement across scorer families (permeation), and a range of point estimates across chambers (cohort-juniority) all answer "does the effect replicate?" — not "does the measure mean the same thing in each population?" The two are different questions in every one of these literatures, and the second is the one Treiman 1977, Gowen–Fosse–Winship 2023 and the AERA/APA/NCME *Standards* ask.

**P8 — Preregistration and blinding buy S10 something the comparator literatures cannot buy back, but they are not the guarantee that is missing.** Where S10 is ahead, it is ahead on *not fitting the analysis to the result*. Where it is behind, it is behind on *does the instrument measure what it is named* — construct validation, convergent and discriminant correlations, criterion breadth, out-of-sample replication. Two verdicts (new-measure, register-predates) say this explicitly. Worth stating once in §3 as a scoping sentence, because it pre-empts the referee who reads the preregistration and then asks for reliability.

**P9 — Clustering is still at the wrong unit in two arms.** Prevalence clusters on segments though 2,340 segments come from 1,123 speakers and drafting is an office-level habit; chase-and-flight treats 40 words as 40 exchangeable units including a morphological pair (advocating/advocates). The study's own record notes it has been bitten three times by this. Both fixes are free.

**P10 — Uncalibrated continuous vendor outputs are carrying load in two arms.** `fraction_ai` weights the prevalence headline (a 25% haircut, 12.03% → 9.03%) and defines the evasion arm's operating point. One calibration experiment serves both, and the floor argument does *not* protect a fraction-weighted estimator the way it protects a binary flag rate — worth saying in the text regardless.

**P11 — S10's honesty conventions are a genuine differentiator and are being under-sold as footnotes.** Retracted nulls, quarantined superseded runs, MDEs attached to nulls, "hypothesis not finding" framing, naming its own earlier figure an error, disclosing that a robustness family is not a replication family, flagging unclustered SEs in place. Across all seven surveys this behaviour is named as above comparator practice — repeatedly, and by literatures that do not otherwise agree with each other. It should be a stated methodological posture in §3 with the instances cross-referenced, not scattered.

### One closing observation for §3

Across all seven surveys, the same asymmetry recurs and is worth stating once, plainly: **S10 is ahead of its adjacent fields wherever the question is "did you fit the analysis to the result?" and behind them wherever the question is "does the instrument measure what you named it?"** Preregistration, blinding, quarantined superseded runs, retracted nulls, MDEs on nulls, and discovery/confirmation separation are all above comparator practice, in some cases without precedent. Reliability figures, convergent and discriminant correlations, criterion breadth, human gold standards, transportable scoring, measurement invariance and out-of-sample replication are the standing entry fees the study has not yet paid. That asymmetry is not a flaw in the study's design; it is what happens when a study is built by someone with preregistration instincts and no measurement-validation checklist. Twenty-four of the twenty-six blocking gaps are computable from what is already committed.
